query: Research on refractory multicomponent alloys has emphasized exceptional strength at room and elevated temperatures, while mechanical assessment has relied mainly on compression and has included relatively few tensile studies. WFeNiMo fragments released more chemical energy than tungsten-alloy fragments in thin-steel-target penetration tests, and HfZrTiTa0.53 was reported at 786 MPa yield strength, 1314 MPa compressive strength, and 13.5% terminal strain. This evidence establishes strength and energetic promise but leaves limited tensile ductility, load-bearing reliability, and processability unresolved. Subject to preserving strength and impact-triggered energy release, what single testable hypothesis identifies an intervention for HfZrTiTa0.53 that could improve tensile ductility and uniform elongation? Include the intervention, causal mechanism, directional or quantitative outcomes relative to the reported baseline, the applicable temperature, loading mode, and strain-rate limits, prior evidence from the cited studies, and matched compression, tension, and impact tests with a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Minor interstitial micro-alloying of HfZrTiTa0.53 with 0.2–0.5 at.% boron, followed by a 1200 °C/12 h homogenisation and water-quench, will raise room-temperature uniform tensile elongation (εu) by ≥50 % (to ≥12 %) and total elongation to ≥20 %, while keeping 0.2 % offset yield strength within ±5 % of the 786 MPa baseline and preserving impact-triggered chemical-energy release (±10 %).
generation.material_initial_state: Vacuum-arc–melted as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory multicomponent alloy, grain size ≈50–80 µm, single BCC phase, reported σy ≈ 786 MPa, σc ≈ 1314 MPa, εt ≈ 13.5 % at 298 K.
generation.intervention: Add 0.2–0.5 at.% B during melting, then homogenise 12 h/1200 °C in vacuum and water-quench.
generation.conditions: Tests at 298 K ±5 K; (i) uniaxial tension and compression at quasi-static 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹; (ii) ballistic thin-steel-target impact at 1.5 ± 0.1 km s⁻¹. Effect expected to hold up to 600 °C and ≤10³ s⁻¹ strain rate.
generation.structural_mediator: Boron segregates to grain boundaries and forms sub-micrometre (Hf,Zr,Ti,Ta)-borides that (a) increase grain-boundary cohesion, (b) Zener-pin grain growth to ≈10–20 µm, and (c) raise work-hardening via Orowan bowing.
generation.mechanism: Stronger, cleaner grain boundaries delay intergranular crack initiation, while grain refinement and dispersed borides enhance slip transfer and back-stress hardening, giving higher uniform plasticity without sacrificing the BCC lattice friction stress that controls strength. Limited B keeps boride volume fraction low, so adiabatic-shear-band–driven oxidation during impact—and thus chemical-energy release—remains essentially unchanged.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline alloy: (1) εu increases from ~8 % (estimated) to ≥12 %; (2) εt rises from 13.5 % to ≥20 %; (3) σy stays 750–825 MPa; (4) σc stays 1.25–1.35 GPa; (5) exothermic light-output/temperature rise of fragments in impact tests changes by ≤10 %.
generation.baseline: HfZrTiTa0.53: σy = 786 MPa, σc = 1314 MPa, εt = 13.5 % (compression data dominant; limited tensile data). WFeNiMo fragments show higher chemical energy release than commercial W alloy.
generation.boundary: Benefit declines above 600 °C (boron desegregation) or for B >0.7 at.% (excess borides embrittle). Effect may disappear at strain rates >10³ s⁻¹ where adiabatic heating dominates failure.
generation.uncertainty: Optimal B content and heat-treat time may vary; excessive oxygen or uncontrolled boride coarsening could negate ductility gains. No prior tensile dataset for this exact alloy, so baseline εu is inferred.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two 50 g ingots: (A) baseline HfZrTiTa0.53, (B) same +0.3 at.% B. Apply identical melting, casting into copper moulds, then homogenise only sample B at 1200 °C/12 h, quench. Machine ASTM E8 sub-size tensile and compression specimens and 5 mm cubic ballistic fragments.
measurements: Room-temperature tensile true stress–strain curves → σy, εu, εt
Ballistic impact tests into 3 mm 4130 steel targets → high-speed imaging, fragment temperature, post-mortem calorimetry for chemical energy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if ANY one of the following is observed for sample B relative to sample A: (i) εu increases by <50 %, OR εt <20 %; (ii) σy decreases by >10 %; (iii) chemical-energy release (measured heat rise) decreases by >15 %.
